newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast Alaskan crude rises after cargo sale.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast Alaskan crude rises after cargo sale.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast Alaskan crude rose Wednesday after a full cargo sold midday at a 10-cent increase over the last deal done, traders said.
BP sold 300,000 barrels of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude to a major California refiner for April delivery at $1.00 a barrel under April WTI.
The deal, confirmed by both sides, tightened the differential from its previous level of minus $1.10, the price of a cargo sold in mid-February.
ANS outright prices ranged $20/20.20 a barrel, up 25 cents from Tuesday on a combination of higher diffs and a 15-cent increase in basis WTI.
Line 63 prices stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05, with two deals heard done Friday at postings plus $1.00. The deals comprised 1,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) of crude for March delivery.
Some sellers claimed the price for Line 63 could rise if more of the diluent grade was needed to push a glut of heavy crudes from production fields to Los Angeles refineries.
Kern River heavy crude stayed steady after falling two days ago, with prices talked 13.84/14.04 a barrel, traders said.
Chevron said the number four crude unit at its El Segundo plant returned to service recently, only a few days after its scheduled return.
The unit had forced more crude into the market, traders said.
